title: Pullback of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of
schemes, with coefficient rings $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$
([sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]) and categories of module objects
$\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]). The *pullback of module objects* is

$$
f^*:=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})\colon
\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X},
$$

where the transport ([sk-def-sfb-transport]) $\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})$ makes $f^*_{\Ab}M$ an
$f^*\Lambda_Y$-module through the strong monoidal structure of the pullback
$f^*_{\Ab}$ of abelian sheaves ([def-sfb-finite-upper-star], [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]), and
$\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}$ extends scalars ([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars])
along $\alpha_f\colon f^*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$ ([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]). Thus

$$
f^*M=\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}M,
$$

the ringed-topos pullback. The functor $f^*$ is additive.

proof.text: Put $F=f^*_{\Ab}$, $R=\Lambda_Y$ and $S=\Lambda_X$. The rings $R,S$ are the commutative pulled-back coefficient rings of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the abelian-sheaf inverse image of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] with its strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]. It preserves commutative ring objects by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided], so $FR$ is commutative. Apply [def-sfb-modobj-transport]: an $R$-module $(M,\gamma_M)$ is sent to the $FR$-module $FM$ with action $FR\otimes FM\xrightarrow{\mu^F}F(R\otimes M)\xrightarrow{F\gamma_M}FM$, and a module map $u$ is sent to $Fu$. Thus the first factor has exactly the coefficient ring required for extension along $\alpha_f$.

source.place: display defining the composite and paragraph defining mapMod

proof.text: The current statement of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] defines $\alpha_f$ as the component at $\Lambda$ of $f^*\circ p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ and explicitly asserts that it is a morphism of ring objects. Its source is $f^*p_Y^*\Lambda=FR$ with the transported strong-monoidal ring structure used in step 1, and its target is $p_X^*\Lambda=S$. Thus extension is along this same $\alpha_f:FR\to S$; no different coefficient comparison is substituted. Abelian sheaves form an abelian category by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; in particular the coequalizer of $a,b:A\rightrightarrows B$ exists as $\operatorname{coker}(a-b)$, since a map kills $a-b$ exactly when it equalizes $a,b$. The sheaf tensor is symmetric and both tensor factors preserve colimits by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. All the hypotheses of [def-sfb-modobj-extension] therefore hold for $FR\to S$. Its coequalizer construction defines $E=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}$, acting on maps by the maps induced by $S\otimes-$. Composing $E$ with the transport of step 1 defines a functor on the stated module categories. On objects it is exactly $S\otimes_{FR}FM=\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}M$. This uses the given ring morphism and the coequalizer construction, and does not choose an inverse to $\alpha_f$.

source.place: definition of extension along alpha_f and the tensor formula

proof.text:
We spell out the elementary additive-adjoint calculation used below. If $L\dashv T$ between preadditive categories and $T$ is additive, the adjunction transpose $h\mapsto T(h)\eta_A$ is injective. For $u,v:A\to B$, naturality of the unit gives
$$T(L(u+v))\eta_A=\eta_B(u+v)=\eta_Bu+\eta_Bv=T(Lu+Lv)\eta_A.$$
Thus $L(u+v)=Lu+Lv$. Also $L(0)=L(0+0)=L(0)+L(0)$, so cancellation in the abelian group $\Hom(LA,LB)$ gives $L(0)=0$; negatives then follow from $0=L(0)=L(u+(-u))=Lu+L(-u)$. For abelian sheaves the pushforward $f_*^{\Ab}$ of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] is additive directly: at $V$ its map is the original map at $V\times_YX$, so it preserves the sectionwise sum. Apply the displayed calculation to the adjunction [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction]. This proves that $F=f^*_{\Ab}$ is additive.

source.place: final sentence: additivity, abelian inverse image factor

proof.text:
The inclusion of abelian sheaves into abelian presheaves preserves sums, which are defined sectionwise. Its left adjoint, the sheafification of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], is additive by the calculation of step 3. Consequently the tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] is additive in either variable: it is the additive sheafification of the objectwise $\mathbf Z$-tensor. For example, on pure tensors $(1\otimes(u+v))(x\otimes m)=x\otimes(um+vm)=x\otimes um+x\otimes vm$, and, for maps $a,b:L\to L'$, $((a+b)\otimes1)(x\otimes m)=(ax+bx)\otimes m=ax\otimes m+bx\otimes m$. Pure tensors generate the objectwise tensor products, so both identities hold on all sections before sheafification, and additive sheafification preserves them. For module maps $u,v:M\to N$, the defining equation of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] is closed under addition:
$$(u+v)\gamma_M=u\gamma_M+v\gamma_M=\gamma_N(R\otimes u)+\gamma_N(R\otimes v)=\gamma_N(R\otimes(u+v)).$$
The zero and negative maps are linear because $0\gamma_M=0=\gamma_N(R\otimes0)$ and $(-u)\gamma_M=-u\gamma_M=-\gamma_N(R\otimes u)=\gamma_N(R\otimes(-u))$. Composition is bilinear on underlying sheaves, so these are the usual preadditive module categories. The transport [def-sfb-modobj-transport] acts on underlying morphisms by $F$, hence step 3 proves that this transport is additive as well.

source.place: final sentence: additive structures and transport factor

proof.text:
Finally, write $q_M:S\otimes M\to EM$ for the coequalizer map defining extension in [def-sfb-modobj-extension], now for any $FR$-module $M$. For parallel module maps $u,v:M\to N$, that node's rule on morphisms and the tensor additivity of step 4 give
$$E(u+v)q_M=q_N(S\otimes(u+v))=q_N(S\otimes u)+q_N(S\otimes v)=(Eu+Ev)q_M.$$
The universal property of the coequalizer makes precomposition with $q_M$ injective: two maps out of $EM$ inducing the same map out of $S\otimes M$ are its same unique factorization. Thus $E(u+v)=Eu+Ev$. The composite $f^*=E\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ preserves sums because each factor does. This proves the last clause without invoking any assertion of exactness of module pullback.

source.place: final sentence: extension factor and composite are additive

proof_origin.place: construction and final additivity sentence, expanded by transport, the defining coequalizer, and explicit additive-adjoint calculation
